chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: The enemy is applying a debuff, not attacking, so Block this turn buys me nothing — every point of Coral Guard would expire unused. That turns the turn into a pure damage question against a 32 HP Shrinker Beetle with no Block. I led with Gorou — General's War Banner (1 energy) because its +3 to my next Attack is the only card that multiplies rather than adds, and I want that rider on my biggest hit. Then All Streams Flow to the Sea for 1: base 9, plus the Charge bank of 8 read at one point per two Charge for +4, plus the Banner's +3, for 16. Then the free Gorou — Inuzaka All-Round Defense for 6, which costs no energy and only exhausts a card I had no other use for. That is 22 of 32. My third energy went to Water's Edge for 6 more, bringing the total to 28 and leaving the Beetle at 4 HP with two Hydro applications on it. The 4 Block from the Banner is incidental and irrelevant against a debuff intent, but the card was worth its cost for the damage rider alone.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes — a Pearl Barrage line. Pearl Barrage for 1, exhausting a Coral Guard (cost 1) since Block is dead this turn, gives 5 plus whatever the total exhausted cost scales to; on the most generous reading of 'scales with the total cost' that is still a small number next to a 16-damage All Streams. I also weighed Bake-Kurage first: 1 energy for a summon, +1 Charge and Burst +5. The extra Charge would only push All Streams from 16 to 16 or 17 depending on rounding at one point per two Charge, and spending a full energy to maybe add a point while losing a 6-damage card is a bad trade on a turn where I am chasing a 32 HP kill window. The Bake-Kurage line is the right one if I expect the fight to run long; I do not, because I can put the Beetle to 4. I briefly considered banking energy into Coral Guard as insurance against the debuff being something that hurts later, but Block does not defend against debuffs.
q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up all defense and all setup. Three Coral Guards and 15 potential Block go unplayed, so if the debuff is followed next turn by a real attack I face it at 62 HP with nothing up. It gave up the Bake-Kurage summon, which means no persistent body, no Charge accumulation for future All Streams, and no Burst progress — I spent the Charge bank rather than growing it. It gave up Tactical Retreat's card selection, though with 3 energy already committed and a random discard attached, drawing was not attractive. And it left the Beetle alive at 4 HP rather than converting the turn into anything durable, so the whole line is a bet that I close next turn.
q4_different_intent: Yes, substantially. Against a telegraphed single-hit attack the Coral Guards become live and the calculus changes: I would likely still lead Banner into All Streams for the 16, but the free Inuzaka for 6 plus a Coral Guard for 5 Block would compete with Water's Edge depending on the printed damage number — a big hit would pull me toward Banner's 4 Block plus one or two Coral Guards and only the free attack. Against a multi-hit or heavy attack I would abandon the race entirely and play two or three Coral Guards. Against an intent to buff itself or summon reinforcements I would go harder on tempo and consider Bake-Kurage to build Charge for a longer fight. The debuff intent is precisely what makes Block worthless and makes the all-in damage line correct.
